bugs.summary: Cleaning up Internationalization section in R-exts
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
I think the R-exts section 1.8 (Internationalization) could go for a fresh look.

Some things I found confusing or that look incorrect:

 - Defining dngettext as a macro that ignores domain. Is there a reason not to use the "normal" dngettext as described in the GNU gettext manual (https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/html_node/Plural-forms.html)? In particular the advice in R-exts to define dngettext as a macro that splits on N > 1 seems to contradict the advice in the GNU manual about pluralization depending on the different uses of plurals in different languages, and the nplurals/plural parameters for gettext.

 - We are advised in 1.8.1 to run xgettext to get the pkg.pot file for the src/ translations, then in 1.8.3, we are advised to `touch` src/pkg.pot before running tools::update_pkg_po(). Only one of these is necessary (personally I find using tools::update_pkg_po() easier to remember as it allows me to stay within R for more of the development workflow). 

 - So far in my translation workflow, tools::update_pkg_po() has been my workhorse. I think centering this function in the discussion first, and then mentioning its component helpers (tools::xgettext2pot(), tools::xgettext(), tools::checkPoFile(), etc.) as ways to dive deeper, would be more instructive/actionable for developers.

 - A typo: tools::checkPofile should be tools::checkPoFile

I'm happy to have a go at working on a patch; raising here first to get R-core feedback first before moving forward with that.

Also noticed today:

tools::udpate_pkg_po uses a call to command-line xgettext with --keyword=N_ as well as --keyword=_:

https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/36219223cff4fedfc7c4e096d7afd187aaa53e14/src/library/tools/R/translations.R#L180

This N_ isn't mentioned anywhere in R-exts but it appears to be defined in the R source as being a xgettext_noop wrapper (which is also hinted in the GNU manual).

Is this intended to be exposed to package developers, or is this part only in tools::update_pkg_po to handle the case when it is run for `base` translations?
comments.creator: michaelchirico4
